messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: high egress error rate detected for service `redwood-api` in us-east-2 (AZ: az2). Alert threshold: >30% 5m. PagerDuty: oncall-network.
sara: acked, I'm on it. grabbing logs from NAT and route tables.
miguel: paging miguel for network assist — @miguel are you available? :raised_hand:
miguel: here. seeing big TCP RST spikes for clients coming from az2 private subnets to external APIs. some flows succeed intermittently.
julia: any recent infra changes? terraform apply earlier today targeted infra/networking/us-east-2. @ben did you run anything?
ben: I applied a patch to standardize route-table associations across AZs at 09:12, but I didn't touch NACLs. I rolled out a small host route tweak but it passed plan checks.
sara: grabbing route tables now. output snippet:
```
# aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=tag:Name,Values=rtb-private-us-east-2a
Routes:
  - DestinationCidrBlock: 0.0.0.0/0
    Target: nat-0a1b2c3d (stale-nat-az1)
Associations:
  - SubnetId: subnet-priv-az2
```
sara: wait — private subnet in az2 is pointing at a NAT that's in az1 (nat-0a1b2c3d). That shouldn't be allowed by our HA model; we expect per-AZ NAT. Could be sticky route propagation from the earlier change.
miguel: checking NAT health checks. NAT nat-0a1b2c3d shows high error rates and is in 'impaired' state per metrics. There's also a DENY NACL rule applied to subnet-priv-az2 that blocks ephemeral ports 1024-65535 from egress randomly.
nicole: how did DENY end up on the NACL? we don't manage that via the standard NACL module.
ben: I did touch route-table associations but not NACLs. I see an automated cleanup job (infra-bot) pushed a NACL update to remove stale CIDRs at 09:15 — maybe a bad rule slipped in.
infra-bot: Deploy job #deploy-7402: applied `nacl-cleanup` on us-east-2 at 09:15. Changes: added rule 100: DENY TCP 1024-65535 from 0.0.0.0/0 to subnet-priv-az2 (intended for dr_test, mistakenly targeted prod tag filter).
sara: ok that's a smoking gun: two independent issues — route table pointing to wrong NAT (fails cross-AZ path) and a NACL DENY on high ports. Combined they create partial egress blackhole for az2.
julia: impact assessment: services in az2 private subnets report 40-60% external request failures. Internal LB between AZs still responds but outbound calls to 3rd-party APIs fail.
customer-success: we're getting customer tickets for timeouts in ingestion pipelines and webhook deliveries. Priority customers in EU experiencing delayed callbacks.
ops-lead: immediate mitigation plan: 1) remove DENY NACL rule from subnet-priv-az2 2) update route table association to point to nat-a-az2 (new nat) or create a replacement NAT if missing 3) failover traffic to nat-a-az2 and monitor.
miguel: executing step 1 now. command:
```
# aws ec2 replace-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id nacl-0xabc123 --rule-number 100 --egress --rule-action allow --cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --protocol tcp
```
miguel: DENY removed, replaced with explicit ALLOW for ephemeral ports. starting to see drop in RSTs.
sara: step 2: I see nat-b-az2 available (nat-1f2e3d4c) but it wasn't associated in route-table. I'll re-point route 0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-1f2e3d4c.
ben: confirming — do it. make change as a small, rollbackable update.
sara: command run:
```
# aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-0abc --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --nat-gateway-id nat-1f2e3d4c
```
sara: route updated. propagating.
infra-bot: route-propagation-monitor: route-change detected for rtb-0abc, propagation complete in 8s.
miguel: pings to external endpoints from az2 tasks return success now. error rate down to ~3%.
julia: rolling window check for 15m. re-evaluating customer impact and paging backlog.
ops-lead: start canary traffic and slowly ramp. Also schedule a postmortem to figure out why nacl-cleanup targeted prod. tag filter issue.
customer-success: notified top 5 impacted customers with temporary mitigation and ETA for full RCA.
ben: root cause notes so far: bad `nacl-cleanup` job targeting incorrect tag filter + route-table drift after terraform apply created cross-AZ reference to nat in az1. Likely caused by subtle tag mismatch in resource names used by the route module.
sara: on-call handoff incoming — @julia you'll be primary for the follow-up and RCA. I'm taking notes and will attach runbook commands to the ticket.
julia: on it. I'll coordinate with infra team to revert the cleanup job to a canary and add stricter tag checks. Also will add automated guardrail: reject NACL changes that add DENY egress-wide rules to prod private subnets.
ops-lead: timeline summary for postmortem:
- 09:12 terraform apply route-table changes
- 09:15 infra-bot nacl-cleanup applied DENY rule to subnet-priv-az2
- 09:18 alert triggered, high egress error rate
- 09:20 mitigation started (DENY removed)
- 09:24 route updated to nat-1f2e3d4c
- 09:32 error rate back to normal (<5%)

Please add any missing notes. We'll publish an incident report and customer follow-ups within 3 business days. :memo:
ben: I'll also add a CI check to ensure route-module outputs explicit az-level nat ids instead of best-effort lookup.
nicole: adding post-incident tasks to backlog and tagging relevant owners.
infra-bot: Incident ticket INC-2026-0453 created and linked to this thread. CI job id for fix: ci/infra-guard-129.
julia: thanks everyone. closing out live mitigation — leaving thread open for postmortem content. :thumbsup:
